method: Unchanged original BlockPistonBase (app, sticky 29 / normal 33), BlockPistonExtension (apq, 34), BlockPistonMoving (apr, 36) and TileEntityPiston (aps) plus the redstone blocks of redstone-reference.json run inside a real World (ahb, allocated without its constructor) with real Chunk (apx) objects. Native: World.setBlock, setBlockMetadataWithNotify, notifyBlocksOfNeighborChange, setTileEntity / getTileEntity / removeTileEntity, World.updateEntities (the tile-entity loop and TileEntityPiston.updateEntity), Block drops, power queries. Replaced: WorldServer scheduled ticks and WorldServer.addBlockEvent / sendQueuedBlockEvents (copied: two ArrayLists swapped by index, BlockEventData.equals de-duplication against the list being filled, delivery through the native Block.onBlockEventReceived), getTotalWorldTime, getGameRules, playSoundEffect / spawnEntityInWorld (recorded), getEntitiesWithinAABB (a scripted list that is empty in every piston scenario: entity pushing is not exercised), lighting. Per tick: scripted events, world time + 1, tickUpdates, sendQueuedBlockEvents, World.updateEntities. Scenario events: place, air, use, placepiston (id, placer x/y/z feet position and yaw; setBlock(id,0,3) then onBlockPlacedBy, 1.62 eye height) plus the redstone events (entity/collide, cauldron, ...). Per tick: changed region cells [x,y,z,id,meta]; te: every TileEntityPiston in the loaded list [x,y,z,storedBlock,storedMeta,facing,extending,renderHead,progress,lastProgress]; the call log: E,op; s,x,y,z,id,meta,flags; m,x,y,z,meta,flags; n,x,y,z,source; t,x,y,z,id,delay,priority; u,x,y,z,id; b,x,y,z,id,event,param addBlockEvent; v,x,y,z,id,event,param delivered; r,0|1 its result; k,x,y,z setTileEntity; K,x,y,z removeTileEntity; p,name sound; e,item dropped item; T world tick. sounds [tick,x,y,z,name,volume,pitch]; drops [tick,x,y,z,item,count,damage]; pending ticks; queued: block events still in the list being filled; rng: world Random nextInt() after the run. blocks.pistonProps rows [id, hardness == -1, getMobilityFlag, ITileEntityProvider, material air] for every registered id below 256.

scenarios.name: push-single
scenarios.note: normal piston pushes one stone east and retracts leaving it

scenarios.name: sticky-pull-single
scenarios.note: sticky piston pushes one stone east and pulls it back

scenarios.name: push-12
scenarios.note: twelve stones are pushed

scenarios.name: push-13-fails
scenarios.note: thirteen stones cannot be pushed: canExtend is false, nothing is queued

scenarios.name: push-12-race-13th
scenarios.note: twelve stones, lever on queues the event, a thirteenth stone is placed in the same tick: the delivered event fails

scenarios.name: push-12-plus-torch
scenarios.note: twelve stones then a torch at the thirteenth cell: the torch is broken and dropped, the line moves

scenarios.name: immovable-blocks
scenarios.note: lanes: obsidian, bedrock, chest, extended piston, stone behind obsidian, retracted piston, lone piston head, plain stone control

scenarios.name: push-drops
scenarios.note: a mobility-1 block in front of each piston (flowers, wire, levers, repeater, torches, button) is broken: Block.dropBlockAsItem draws and item entities

scenarios.name: normal-pulses
scenarios.note: normal pistons with lever pulses of 1 to 6 ticks; stone in front. Short sticky pulses hit the moving-block branch of the 1.7.10 retraction

scenarios.name: sticky-pulses
scenarios.note: sticky pistons with lever pulses of 1 to 6 ticks; stone in front. Short sticky pulses hit the moving-block branch of the 1.7.10 retraction

scenarios.name: sticky-pull-exceptions
scenarios.note: extended sticky pistons retract with a torch, retracted piston, extended piston, obsidian, stone, wire or air in front of the head

scenarios.name: quasi-connectivity
scenarios.note: redstone blocks at (x,y+2,z), (x,y+1,z-1), (x,y+1,z+1) and (x-1,y+1,z) power the piston only after a block update; removal does not retract until another update

scenarios.name: piston-redstone-circuits
scenarios.note: normal and sticky pistons move a redstone block along a wire/lamp line (power returns when the moved block lands); a stone pushed against a torch's wall

scenarios.name: double-extender
scenarios.note: sticky piston A pushes retracted sticky piston B and a stone; B is then powered at its new position and extends; both retract

scenarios.name: double-extender-blocked
scenarios.note: B extends first, then A cannot push the extended B; retract B, then A pushes it

scenarios.name: normal-flicker
scenarios.note: rapid lever toggles across consecutive ticks and several toggles inside one tick (the extend/retract events are re-checked against the power at delivery)

scenarios.name: sticky-flicker
scenarios.note: rapid lever toggles across consecutive ticks and several toggles inside one tick (the extend/retract events are re-checked against the power at delivery)

scenarios.name: placement-orientation
scenarios.note: BlockPistonBase.determineOrientation for placers at four yaws, above (looking down), below (looking up), 45 degrees and a far diagonal

scenarios.name: place-powered
scenarios.note: pistons placed next to powered redstone blocks update at metadata 0 first, then again after onBlockPlacedBy sets the orientation

scenarios.name: head-and-base-removal
scenarios.note: breaking an extended piston's head drops the base piston; removing the base removes the orphan head

scenarios.name: bounds-top
scenarios.note: up-facing pistons at y 252 and 253 with and without a stone in front: a push into y 255 is refused (target y >= 255 fails canExtend)

scenarios.name: bounds-bottom
scenarios.note: down-facing pistons at y 1 (target y 0 refused), y 2 and y 3: pushes down need the target y > 0

scenarios.name: normal-all-facings
scenarios.note: normal pistons facing down, up, north, south, west and east push (and for sticky pull) a stone

scenarios.name: sticky-all-facings
scenarios.note: sticky pistons facing down, up, north, south, west and east push (and for sticky pull) a stone

scenarios.name: event-order-four
scenarios.note: one redstone block placed between four up-facing pistons queues four events in neighbour-notification order, extends, retracts and re-extends

scenarios.name: event-order-chain
scenarios.note: a redstone block beside the first piston of a chain: the pushed blocks' neighbour updates queue further events in the second delivery pass

scenarios.name: power-sources
scenarios.note: pistons powered by adjacent wire, a repeater output, a block strongly powered by a wall lever and wire on a block beside them

scenarios.name: clock-drives-pistons
scenarios.note: a four-repeater ring started by a one-tick redstone block pulse; two tap repeaters drive a normal and a sticky piston on every pass of the pulse

scenarios.name: retract-from-extended
scenarios.note: extended pistons present at the start retract on power loss: normal leaves the stone, sticky pulls it (horizontal, up and down)

scenarios.name: push-plate-lamp
scenarios.note: a pressure plate (needs a supporting block) and a lamp next to a redstone block are pushed and, for the sticky piston, pulled back
